indication.text: Long-term, once-daily maintenance bronchodilator treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema. Not indicated for asthma or for acute deteriorations of COPD.

citations.quote: ARCAPTA NEOHALER is a long-acting beta2-agonist indicated for long-term, once-daily maintenance bronchodilator treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema.
ARCAPTA NEOHALER is not indicated to treat acute deteriorations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [see *Warnings and Precautions (5.2)*].

target_moa.text: Indacaterol is a long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonist that acts locally in the lung as a bronchodilator; stimulation of intracellular adenylyl cyclase increases cyclic AMP, causing relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle.

citations.quote: Indacaterol is a long-acting \beta_2-adrenergic agonist.
When inhaled, indacaterol acts locally in the lung as a bronchodilator.
Increased cyclic AMP levels cause relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle.
The active component of ARCAPTA NEOHALER is indacaterol maleate, a (R) enantiomer. Indacaterol maleate is a selective beta2-adrenergic agonist.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>2% and more common than placebo) are cough, oropharyngeal pain, nasopharyngitis, headache and nausea. For 75 mcg vs placebo: cough 6.5% vs 4.5%, oropharyngeal pain 2.2% vs 0.7%, nasopharyngitis 5.3% vs 2.7%, headache 5.1% vs 2.5%, nausea 2.4% vs 0.9%. Most common serious adverse reactions were COPD exacerbation, pneumonia, angina pectoris, and atrial fibrillation.

detail.text: WARNING: ASTHMA-RELATED DEATH. Long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonists (LABA) increase the risk of asthma-related death. A placebo-controlled study with salmeterol showed an increase in asthma-related deaths; this is considered a class effect of LABA including indacaterol.

summary.text: Standard 505(b)(1) NDA for indacaterol maleate (Arcapta Neohaler) 75 mcg for COPD. The original NDA received a Complete Response letter on October 16, 2009; Novartis submitted a complete response on October 1, 2010. A Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee met March 8, 2011 and recommended approval of the 75 mcg dose (13 yes, 4 no). Approval was supported by a REMS with a Medication Guide and communication plan; no post-marketing study commitments were required.
